summary: A Neighborhood Stories feature on local firefighters at Centerville Fire Station 6, showing how the job has expanded from fighting fires to using technology such as AR helmets, drones, AI and robotics. It shares personal accounts of rescues, mental health challenges, community education, medical work, inter-agency collaboration and ongoing training. The piece argues firefighting is increasingly about precision, prediction and prevention as well as courage.
one_line: Profile of Centerville firefighters showing how technology, training, community outreach and personal bravery are reshaping modern firefighting.
key_facts: On September 12, 2023, the alarm sounded at Centerville Fire Station 6, where Fire Chief Melissa Carter, a 15-year veteran, was among the responders.
Chief Melissa Carter said, "We're not just fighting fires anymore... We're data analysts, we're tech operators, and above all, we are a mobile rapid response unit."
Firefighter Aaron Lee said AR helmets let crews see through smoke during the High Street blaze last November, showing structural weak points and survivor locations.
On December 8, 2023, Lieutenant Gabriela Rodriguez's team used drones with sensors and water hoses to contain a large chemical plant fire without a single injury.
AI systems in fire stations analyze data from city sensors to predict and pinpoint where fire risks are highest.
Remotely operated robots can navigate rubble and extract victims while controlled from a safe distance.
Rookie firefighter James O'Connell rescued an elderly couple from a fully engulfed house fire on Maple Street last October, entering through a first-floor window despite roof collapse risk.
Psychologist Dr. Renee Syed says firefighters face traumatic situations that can lead to PTSD, anxiety, and depression.
Firefighter Jamal Patterson described a community engagement initiative launched October 1, 2023, with workshops, school programs and VR simulations.
Paramedic and firefighter Lila Nguyen, who joined in February 2024, stresses medical training to stabilize victims until they reach a hospital.

On September 15, 2023, Captain Derek Huang's team responded to a multi-vehicle accident with intense flames on Interstate 405, aided by joint training and established protocols with law enforcement and EMS.
Firefighter trainee Kiera Jones, graduating in March 2024, is learning to pilot drones and interpret heat maps alongside traditional firefighting.
